- **⭐⭐⭐ CEO-1223 — LON ASKED WHETHER THE rtccb VENEER IS SPECIFIC TO THE C RUNTIME AND ASKED THE ceo TO VERIFY NO ASM RT CARRIES IT: IT IS NOT C-ONLY (2026-09-23 18:2x–18:3x CDT `date`-read, ceo, measured at SCRIP `e4c313aee`).** Lon, in-chat, verbatim: *"Is the rtccb veneer that saves/restore registers aroung runtime call specific to only the C version. Will you verify no ASM RT has the veneer?"* **THE MECHANISM:** `x86_rtcc_call` picks the mask per callee from ONE table, `x86_rtcc_clob_raw` in `src/templates/x86/x86_asm.h`, whose default for any symbol it does not list is `RTCC_C_ALL` (spill r8 ANCHOR, r9 GVA, r10, r11 to `rtccb+40..64` before the call, reload after); it does not know which callees are asm. Of the 72 `RTX_FUNC` entries in `src/runtime/rtx/*.s`, the table exempts 8 and partly exempts 5. **THE WITNESS (the emitted asm, next-line reload from `rtccb` = veneered):** the 94 committed `.s` artifacts under corpus `demos/` and `benchmarks/` hold 14,813 calls into the asm runtime, 12,862 of them (87%) veneered across 38 distinct asm entries (heaviest `rt_pl_tr_unwind` 4654, `rt_pl_dop_mkc` 1395, `rt_pl_dop_unify` 868, `rt_subscript_var` 559, `rt_assign_var` 533); nine benchmarks compiled fresh at `e4c313aee` read 1,120 of 1,249. The asm files themselves contain no `rtccb` reference: the veneer lives entirely at the emitted call sites. **WHY IT IS THERE TODAY:** `rtx_abi.inc` declares `rax rcx rdx rsi rdi r8 r9 r10 r11` the RTX WORKING SET, "free at every entry", so an asm entry may clobber r8 and r9 and the veneer is protecting live ANCHOR and GVA values. Taking it off the asm runtime is therefore an ABI change, not a table edit: the RTX contract must promise r8/r9 (and r10/r11 while the diagnostics use them) survive every entry, each routine staying off them or saving them itself, and the exemption must then be derived from the `RTX_FUNC` list rather than hand-listed. Put to Lon as a row for the cto, pending his word. First benchmark row in the grid the same sitting: hq_snocone's SncBench 16/16 (SCRIP `5ad13645a`), every Snocone benchmark printing its REF in both modes under all three angles.

The second is `mov r8, [rip+rtccb+40]` (and r9, r10, r11) / `mov [rip+rtccb+40], r8` / `call rt_gc_poll_asm` — **RELOAD, WRITE-BACK, CALL, WITH NO RELOAD AFTER THE CALL AT ALL**, because the poll string was concatenated inside the PRECEDING call's own rtcc bracket and the two brackets interleaved. ⛔⭐ **WHY THAT WORD IS LOAD-BEARING FOR SNOBOL4 SPECIFICALLY, verified to three citations rather than inferred:** `rtccb+40` is NOT a scratch slot. `src/runtime/rtx/rtcc.h:23` sets `RTCC_GLOBAL_R8_ANCHOR 1`, so r8 is a DEDICATED GLOBAL holding `&ANCHOR`; `x86_asm.h:1557` compiles `rtcc_anchor_cmp` against r8 itself on that arm; and `core/core.c:3304` has `ASGNIC_fn` write the anchor value into `rtccb[RTCC_SLOT_R8]` (slot 5, offset 40, pinned by the `static_assert` at `x86_asm.h:349`). **ONE WORD, TWO OWNERS: the caller-saved r8 spill slot and `&ANCHOR`'s authoritative home.** r8 is also SysV argument register 5. That is a concrete route by which inserting a poll changes a SNOBOL4 program's answer with the collector off, it is the coo's hypothesis with the citations now checked, and it is a ROW for hq_snobol4 and the cto rather than a claim of mine. ⛔⭐⭐ **AND I ALMOST PUBLISHED A SEVEN-LANGUAGE ALL-CLEAR OFF A DETECTOR THAT FAILED OPEN ON THE ONE CASE I HAD JUST WATCHED BREAK.** I wrote a line-window reader for the inverted bracket, ran it on the control asm, and it printed `INVERTED=0` on the exact file whose inversion I had read in the diff two minutes earlier: it computed the load positions and then never tested them. Fixed, it fires on the control — and it ALSO fires at the same line on origin HEAD, which means either a pre-existing inversion or a window that conflates two adjacent brackets, and I cannot tell which. **SO THE SWEEP IS NOT PUBLISHED AND THE DETECTOR IS NOT WIRED.** A line window cannot separate adjacent brackets; this wants a bracket parser over the emitted stream, minted as its own row. The general form is the standing hazard from this root's digest — the DETECTOR ARM, the one asserting the old bad behaviour is still detectable, FAILS OPEN and reads as "there was never a bug here" — and the only reason I caught it is that I diffed the asm by eye first, which is ASM-DIFF-FIRST earning its place in the law.

- **CEO-456 (2026-09-09 10:0x CDT, `date`-read) — LON'S ASK ANSWERED: JCON AND ICONX ALLOCATION CHOICES COMPARED WITH THE THREE ZETAS** (`FINDING-2026-09-09-ceo-jcon-and-iconx-allocation-choices-compared-with-scrip-three-zetas.md`, every claim file:line; research agent, read-only). VERDICT: 8 rows AGREE, 4 DIVERGE. Operand results, construct locals, statics and globals: fixed compile-time slots and a static area in all three — ζ-SPINE and ζ-STANDING have two independent precedents. Suspended state: Jcon moves the whole procedure into a heap closure object at the first call; iconx leaves the frame on its stack under a generator marker; SCRIP leaves it on the machine stack pinned to RBP and resumes through the resume record — iconx's scheme, a legitimate LIFO optimisation of Jcon's. **BOTH REFERENCES DERIVE, NEITHER ENUMERATES:** Jcon mints a closure iff the IR contains a resumable succeed or a create (gen_bc.icn:911-921); iconx decides nothing at compile time and pushes a generator marker only when a suspend executes (interp.r:613, :731) — the precedent for RULES.md:173. **THE ONE PRESENT DEFECT IS CO-EXPRESSIONS:** iconx copies the creator's arguments AND locals BY VALUE into the refresh block and onto the new stack (lmisc.r:39-55, rcoexpr.r:31-52); Jcon shares the creator's variable objects by reference; SCRIP memcpy's `[base, base+frame_bytes)`, which excludes the locals below the base, and `bb_create.cpp:20` saves `rsp` in exactly the `flat_gen` case where the body addresses off `rbp` — hq_S's patchu, mechanism now named. Two hazards to prove: a bounded expression that leaves a callee generator suspended must release its frame at ω or a loop leaks stack (iconx `Op_Unmark`); a variable escaping a dying frame through return/suspend/@ needs iconx's `retderef` discipline (UNVERIFIED in SCRIP). ROUTED: R1–R3 (capture extent, base register from the one selector, by-value) → hq_S now (R2 rides the cto's cut); R4 (`retderef`) → hq_U to measure; R5 (ω release) → the cto's cut; R6 is the cut's gate; R7 (the call-boundary dereference site) → the coo's staging class; R8 (a generator EXPRESSION owns no frame) → hq_V as a rung with a `--dump-zeta` assertion.** **Lon, 2026-09-09 10:1x CDT, in-chat, verbatim: *"You are correct. We diverge because SCRIP is more powerful and hence better."* — the three design divergences (locals and suspended generators on the machine stack, not Jcon's heap; wired ports, not a marker copy) are AFFIRMED as the design; only the co-expression capture is a defect, and the ω release and escape-dereference are measurements pending.**

- **CEO-291 (2026-09-05 11:5x CDT; `date` read 11:52:04 at the MODE rewrite) — LON'S THREE ORDERS IN ONE SITTING: THE CEO TAKES THE ICON SERIAL ROW · THE GLOBAL IS GRANTED · MODE → QUARTET · A FIFTH HQ ROOT.** (1) Lon, verbatim: *"Take the Icon serial row yourself."* — `icon-program-visible-list-serial-burned-by-driver-args-staging-at-startup` CLAIMED:ceo (hq_C told it leaves its lane). MECHANISM, oracle-settled: iconx builds the argument list before `main` ONLY when `main` takes a parameter (`main()` → `list_1(3)` with or without args; `main(args)` → `list_2(3)` and args is `list_1`); SCRIP built it unconditionally since `1d31e2963` removed the nparams gates so HOST could read its arguments — but HOST never needs the list (selector 2 reads the raw command line, selector 3 needs only the count).
